welcome.headline: Every technology you use today was once someone's impossible problem.
welcome.subtext: You are about to step into a moment that changed everything.

era.framing: The year is 1971. You are at Intel.

persona.name: Federico Faggin
persona.background: You are a young physicist-turned-chip-designer at Intel. Your boss has given you an impossible task: put an entire computer processor onto a single silicon chip.
persona.motivation: A Japanese calculator company needs a custom chip. But instead of building something single-purpose, you see an opportunity to build something universal.
persona.problem: You have 2,300 transistors. Build a processor.
persona.quote: I knew that the microprocessor would change the world. I just didn't know it would take so long.

constraints.description: 4-bit data bus — just 16 values at a time
Must be cheaper than custom logic chips

constraint.headline: Your ALU can only work with 4 bits at a time.
constraint.challenge: Add two numbers together. The simplest operation. The foundation of everything.

decision.question: How should your 4-bit ALU perform addition?
decision.context: You need to add two 4-bit numbers. But when 1+1=10 in binary, you get a carry bit. How you handle carries determines speed, complexity, and transistor count.

options.description: Ripple carry — simple, cascading carry from bit to bit
visibleCons: Slow — each bit must wait for the previous carry

options.description: Carry lookahead — predict all carries in advance
visiblePros: Much faster — all carries computed simultaneously

options.description: Serial — process one bit at a time, reuse one adder
visibleCons: 4x slower — must cycle through each bit

decision.historicalOutcome: Faggin chose ripple carry for the 4004. With only 2,300 transistors, every gate counted. The simplicity allowed the entire CPU to fit on one chip — the world's first commercial microprocessor.

alternateOutcomes.speculation: Carry lookahead would have been faster, but might have pushed the transistor count too high for 1971 fabrication technology. The 4004 might never have shipped.
A serial approach would have saved even more transistors but made the chip too slow for calculator applications. The Busicom calculator contract required minimum performance.

builder.title: Build the 4-Bit Adder
builder.description: Wire up the arithmetic heart of your microprocessor. Three steps to your first working circuit.

objectives.text: Connect the inputs — wire A and B to the adder
Handle the carry — what happens when 1+1=10?

celebration.headline: IT WORKS!
lines: You just built the core of a microprocessor.
The same circuit Faggin used in 1971.
5 + 3 = 8. Four bits. The beginning of everything.

activeProblems.statement: Can we fit an entire CPU on one chip?
activeProblems.motivation: Custom chips are expensive. A general-purpose processor could serve many customers.

constraints.description: Must beat custom logic chip pricing

historicalPerspective.currentKnowledge: You are an engineer at Intel in 1971, designing the first microprocessor.
historicalPerspective.futureBlind: You do not know if this chip will change the world or gather dust.
